topics.title: Objective of Revenue Recognition

segments.content: Open with the purpose, not the five steps. Revenue depicts the transfer of promised goods or services to a customer, in the amount the entity expects to be entitled to. Deliver the definition in three pieces, pausing on each: what revenue depicts, what transfers, and how much is recognised. The key words the exam rewards are 'transfer' and 'expects to be entitled to'.
must_say: Revenue depicts the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the entity expects to be entitled to.

beats.anchor: revenue depicts the transfer of promised goods or services

chunks: of promised goods or services to customers
in the amount the entity expects to be entitled to

segments.content: Contrast signing with satisfying. Airbus agreeing to sell aircraft to Cathay Pacific creates a contract but recognises nothing. Revenue arrives when control of the aircraft transfers. Make the single distinguishing feature explicit: an enforceable promise versus a transferred asset.

beats.anchor: signing the contract is not the same as satisfying it

segments.content: Close with the exam-strategy line before asking the question. Say it once, plainly, as advice about the marker rather than as another fact.

payload.text: Writing 'when the contract is signed'. The marker wants transfer of control.

assessment.question: Why is signing a customer contract not enough by itself to recognise revenue?
assessment.expected_answer: Revenue is recognised when the performance obligation is satisfied and control of the promised good or service transfers to the customer.

options.text: Because the contract has not been approved in writing yet
Because control of the promised good or service has not transferred yet
Because the customer has not paid cash yet

assessment.reexplain_guide: Contrast agreeing to deliver an airplane with actually transferring control of it.

payload.stem: Why is signing a contract not enough to recognise revenue?

options.text: The contract is not in writing

topics.loses_marks: Answering 'when the contract is signed'. The marker is looking for transfer of control.

remediation.content: The student is on the cash basis. Re-anchor on the definition already on the board and point out that it never mentions payment.

beats.anchor: revenue is not about when the cash arrives

payload.text: Cash timing does not decide revenue

remediation.content: The student is looking at the paperwork. Use one distant-domain analogy: a signed rental agreement is not the same as handing over the keys.

beats.anchor: signing the rental agreement versus handing over the keys

payload.text: Signed agreement is not handed-over keys

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the two key words already on the board: transfer, and expects to be entitled to.

topics.title: The Connected Five-Step Process

segments.content: Teach the five steps as one chain, not a list. The first four decide what is being accounted for and how much belongs to each promise; the fifth decides when revenue is recorded. Name each link as you reach it.

beats.anchor: the five steps are one connected chain

segments.content: Break the chain deliberately. If the promises are not separated at step two, the allocation at step four is wrong and the revenue at step five is wrong with it. This is the link the exam tests.

beats.anchor: if the promises are not separated the allocation is wrong

payload.text: Miss a separate obligation and every later step inherits the error

topics.loses_marks: Listing the five steps without saying what each one decides. The marker pays for the decision, not the label.

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the chain already on the board and walk two links only.

topics.title: Allocating the Transaction Price

segments.content: Work one example end to end and leave it on the board as the model. A bundle sells for 120,000 SAR with standalone selling prices of 100,000 and 50,000. Show the ratio, then each allocated amount, then the entry. Say every step out loud in order.

beats.anchor: the allocation ratio is each standalone price over the total
add the standalone selling prices together
apply each ratio to the transaction price
the journal entry records the allocation

segments.content: Now run the same procedure with the marks-losing step hidden. Give a second bundle and stop at the ratio, asking the student to supply it. The worked example stays visible beside it as the model.

beats.anchor: now you supply the ratio and the allocated amount

payload.template: Ratio = ___ , so the allocated amount is ___ SAR

assessment.question: A bundle sells for 90,000 SAR. The standalone prices are 40,000 and 20,000. How much is allocated to the first component?
assessment.expected_answer: 60,000 SAR, because 40,000 over 60,000 is two thirds of the 90,000 transaction price.
assessment.reexplain_guide: Return to the pinned worked example and repeat only the ratio step.

topics.loses_marks: Splitting the price evenly instead of by standalone selling price. It costs the whole allocation mark.

remediation.content: Re-anchor on the pinned worked example and repeat the ratio step only.
Work a fresh two-component example beside the pinned one, stating the ratio aloud at each step.

beats.anchor: an even split ignores what each component is worth
